text.tspan: Legal uncertainty and regulatory requirements
Vendor dependence and lock-in risk (limited portability, contract constraints)
Change fatigue and user adoption resistance (frontline reluctance, cultural barriers)
Infrastructure and energy constraints (compute capacity, power availability)
Governance, policy, and operating model gaps (unclear ownership, intake, approvals)
Hallucinations and factual accuracy risk (outputs that are confidently wrong)
Project delays and timeline slippage (longer-than-expected implementation)
Responsible AI and assurance requirements (bias, fairness, explainability, redteaming)
Workforce impact and reskilling challenges (redeployment, training, change management)
Lack of internal alignment or executive sponsorship (conflicting priorities, unclear mandate)
Unclear business case and ROI (difficulty quantifying benefits, uncertain payback)
Model selection and orchestration complexity (choosing and managing multiple models)
Sustainability and carbon footprint concerns (environmental impact of AI workloads)
Lack of AI capability to do the task required (no AI tool available or the one available does not meet our needs)
Data readiness and access issues (quality, fragmentation, compliance barriers)
Integration with legacy systems and workflows (connecting AI to existing tech stack)
Scaling from pilot to production (moving beyond proof-ofconcept)
Shortage of AI skills and expertise (engineering, governance, evaluation roles)
High and unpredictable costs (infrastructure, licensing, evaluation)
Trust, security, privacy, and reputational risk (data leakage, brand exposure)
Thinking about the next 12 months, what 3 top challenges could your company face in the rollout of Generative AI?
